name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default. This ensures keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one click, solving the core keyboard navigation problem without relying on hidden elements that may fail in some browsers. The trade-off is a small permanent UI element, but it’s a standard pattern (like on gov.uk) that improves usability for everyone, not just assistive tech users.

name: Reader
text: A large, high-contrast skip link risks pushing primary content below the fold on small screens, making it harder for *all* users—not just keyboard users—to reach key information quickly. Instead, use a compact skip link that only appears on keyboard focus, paired with a visible focus indicator to avoid confusion for first-time users. Settle this by testing with real screen-reader users on mobile and desktop—if the skip link delays access or obscures content, revert to the compact version.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **hidden skip link** that only appears when focused via keyboard. This keeps the skip link out of sight for mouse users while ensuring keyboard navigators can bypass repetitive content instantly. The trade-off is that sighted keyboard users must tab once to reveal it, but this is a small price for universal access—hidden skip links are a well-supported, low-risk solution that doesn’t clutter the interface for everyone else.

name: Reader
text: The hidden skip link still risks confusing first-time keyboard users who don’t know it exists until they tab—adding a tiny, subtle hint (like a faint outline on the first focusable element) would help. A better alternative is a compact, always-visible skip link that collapses to a small icon on focus, balancing discoverability and screen real estate. Settle it with user testing: measure how often keyboard users miss the hidden link versus how often sighted users complain about the visible one.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a compact, high-contrast skip link that’s always visible but collapses to a small icon when focused—with a subtle focus hint on the first element. Result: EXCAVA pages must support instant keyboard navigation bypass. Owner: accessibility-w1.
